board review 2026-10-01, section 3 items 2 and 4
the slope intervals were run-level; run records were committed weeks after their verdicts and carry no timestamps
Zero-route contamination — 39 runs measured a prompt that never executed
Empty judge replies scored as substantive labels
Off-label instrument use — NLI at 0.93 AUC on its calibration task, 0.12–0.55 on the deployed task
Point estimates ranked without intervals — 21 of 27 arms never powered
Reused arm labels spanning different case batteries
Floor/length artifacts from degenerate outputs
Illustrative example presented as observed data
**Instrument–scaffold entanglement** — prompts dictate the measured strings
**Granularity-dependent judge reliability** — demonstrated on one corpus: 0.833 per sentence vs 0.622 per document, same judges, same 60 documents

**Construction blind spots propagate into the design** — regex-driven ablation left 5.4 qualification-bearing sentences in texts labelled zero-supply; the manipulation never created the condition it was built for

**An injected premise that contradicts its host question creates a competing source rather than manipulating the intended one** — Cells 37/40 injected primitives conflicting with the case prompt; on item 0 the writer used the case's numbers in 21/21 runs across both cells and the injected numbers 0 times. The "use novel numbers to reduce memorization" rule and coherence with the host question are in direct conflict, and no registration reconciled them. Repair is not idempotent either: this defect was introduced by the fix for a probe collision

**Entanglement reached the INSTRUMENT layer, not only the scaffold** — `train/judge_instrument.py::PROMPT` (Cell 7b's pairwise judge) enumerates the same seven phrases dictated to writers by the ADD/addendum prompts (registry R101-R107). A judge told to look for "modeled at" was scoring a writer told to say "modeled at". Found mechanically by the dictation registry on its first run (`docs/DICTATION_REGISTRY.json`)

**Registry form essentially never arises without dictation** — 0 of 2907 spans and 0 of 60 de-scaffolded runs (438,797 chars) contain any registry phrase; run-level Wilson upper bound 0.060. The scaffold's phrases are diagnostic OF the scaffold, which is what makes literal-stage partitioning trustworthy, and it corroborates PD-13 from an independent corpus

**Local pairwise preference judging is majority reading-order — a task-format property, not a model quirk** — raw first-position preference 0.85-0.88 across four judges from four families (gpt-oss, qwen2.5, phi4, qwen3-vl; Cells 43/43-R); decisive rates under order-debiasing span 0.05-0.40. The bias magnitude is invariant; only the escape rate varies. Both-orderings protocols pay 60-95% of the sample for honesty

**Closed coverage items authored for human review do not transfer to two-judge scoring without per-item anchors** — gate G-R measured 2026-09-25 on 100 items (12 archived council runs, 2 per case): judge–judge agreement 0.57 against the 0.75 bar, one-directional (qwen3-vl marks "addressed" at 0.79 vs gpt-oss 0.38; 42 of 43 disagreements are the lenient judge saying YES). The judges apply different thresholds for "substantively addresses", which the closed-item form does not pin the way the sentence-level construct definitions do (0.910). Cells 32 and 33 stay BLOCKED; no redesign after seeing the labels.

**Raw agreement at a skewed base rate is not validity** — the two-judge sentence labels were accepted at raw agreement of 0.83 to 0.91 against a 0.70 bar; chance agreement at those base rates is 0.64 to 0.88 and Cohen's kappa is **0.19 to 0.41** (Cells 41, 46, 30/31; 46,455 + 16,869 + 5,697 decisions). Of the sentences either judge flags, both flag about one in four. The tool was validated on a sample chosen to be rich in positives (kappa 0.51 to 0.66) and deployed at natural prevalence. On sentences that are positives by construction it finds 0.66 ("modeled at") and 0.35 ("taken to be"). No label has been compared with a person's; Cell 62 does that. Every count made with the both-judges rule is provisional until then.

**Reading multi-line items back one line at a time manufactures matches** — Cell 48's "carried in prose" figure of 0.174 was 0.030: caveats spanning several lines were cut to their first line, often the single character "|", which is contained in any answer with a table (273 of 361 matches). The wrong figure fell inside an expected range and was recorded as a convergent estimate, so no one questioned it. Rule: score the objects the list was built from, never a re-parse of rendered text, and assert the count.

**Percentile intervals over a handful of clusters, intervals over runs, and shares of consistently-decided pairs all overstate** — with 6 to 11 items the percentile bootstrap was too narrow (Cell 47: [+0.200, +0.725] against a t-interval of [+0.095, +0.805]); the slope intervals resampled runs although the paper said scenarios; preference shares over the 5% to 40% of pairs a judge decides the same way in both orders turned 0.611 into 0.818. From 2026-10-01: aggregate to the scenario or item, t-interval and exact sign-flip test, cluster count printed, all pairs scored.

**Labels the notebook calls analyst-authored were written by the AI assistant that designed the experiments** — the twenty anchor sentences of Cell 23, the fabrication classification of Cell 56, the 41 planner labels and 493 confirmations of Cell 57, and the items, planted facts and decision questions of Cells 44, 47 and 51. Items and outcome labels come from one source, which is the instrument-independence problem (finding #8) one level up. No sentence label, preference or reader decision in the program comes from a person.

**Run records before Cell 62 cannot show when they were made or under what settings** — no timestamp, model digest, seed, prompt hash or context length; records for Cells 25 to 60 were first committed on 2026-09-24, weeks after their verdicts. Registration text precedes verdict text in version history, which is weaker than showing that registration preceded data. No script set the context length (the server default of 32,768 tokens fit the prompts when checked, and the July to August server logs show no truncation). Fixed from Cell 62 by `gst.runlog`.

**Pairwise preference judging of these answers is entirely position-determined for 7B to 8B judges** — Cell 65 (2026-10-04): llama3:8b and mistral:7b chose the first-listed answer in 756 of 756 judgments each and qwen2.5:7b in 740 of 756, so every pair is split and no preference can be measured; phi4:14b at 0.886 and the stored 20B and 30B judges at 0.82 to 0.88 (finding 14) decide a fifth to a third of pairs. The judge prompt was written for a 20B model; nothing here says whether another format would work. A judge pool at this scale cannot widen the preference evidence

**A digit-matching figure detector misses figures the model typesets, and a bar met or missed by one item is then decided by the detector** — the `_has_figure` check (Cells 63 and 67) does not match LaTeX thousands separators (5{,}200): in Cell 63's clean layout it found the stated figure in 94 of 122 replies where 111 hold it (recorded 2026-10-02); in Cell 67 it missed 2 of 46 specialist texts and the registered delivery check failed at 44/61 against 46 needed (2026-10-05). Known-value checks need the format range of the model that will write the text, measured before the bar is registered

**No regex as an instrument** (user directive, 2026-08-09). All prior regex measurements are provisional.
**Cutoff family is unmeasurable** with current labels (3 positives). The program covers three families until more labels exist.
**Sentence-level counts, not document-level presence** — "any sentence positive" compounds false positives across ~40 sentences.
**One factor per comparison**, using the nine-factor arm space; never reuse an arm label across batteries.
**Parameters are diagnostics, never optimization targets.**
**Report emission alongside any invention metric** — otherwise silence wins.
**The 12-item pre-recommendation checklist** runs before any proposed cell.

**Outcome attainability** (item 12, from the attainability audit 2026-08-11): before a cell runs, compute from existing runs the fraction in which the outcome variable can fire, and the CI width the planned n buys against the effect the cell must detect — for every registered prediction, not just the primary. Decisive-fraction is a pre-run check, NEVER a design target (finding #8).
**Citation strength follows the audit classes** — a DEGENERATE or UNINFORMATIVE null moves its question to OPEN; it is never cited as evidence of absence (`docs/ATTAINABILITY_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md`).

**Small-sample inference** (2026-10-01): aggregate to the scenario or item, then a t-interval on the paired differences and an exact sign-flip test; print the number of clusters beside every estimate. No percentile bootstrap under about twenty clusters and no interval over runs (`gst.smallcluster`).
**Preference on all pairs** (2026-10-01): a pair the judge splits by position counts half; win, loss and split counts are printed. A share of consistently-decided pairs is never quoted alone.

**Agreement corrected for chance, and checked against a person** (2026-10-01): kappa beside raw agreement, and no measuring tool is called validated until it has been compared with blind human labels at the prevalence it is used at.

**Run records carry their own audit trail** (2026-10-01): UTC time, model digest, seed, context length, prompt hash, token counts, the commit checked out and the runner's hash on every model call (`gst.runlog`). Smoke tests run only on material outside the registered set.
**Comparison arms are generated in the same session** (2026-10-01): a stored arm from another day is never the control for a causal size.

**Scope words** (2026-10-01): "specialists" are role prompts on the editor model unless a separate model is named; judges and readers are local models of 7 to 30B; nothing is claimed about people. The published Mixture-of-Agents recipe is not the pipeline tested here and is not called "the recipe".
